[imageid=9912916 medium rep]▪️ Much excitement for The Lord of the Rings: The Return of the King – Trick-Taking Game which was announced for release mid January 2027 from Office Dog. This is the last installment in the series from designer Bryan Bornmueller (The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring – Trick-Taking Game). If you aren't familiar with the series, each game is a multi-chapter game and will essentially walk you through the book's events. The game is cooperative trick-taking and those chapters increase in difficulty as you play through. It is very exciting for Lord of the Rings fans! A game will play 1-4 players in about 20 minutes.
From BGG:

Familiar mechanics, new challenges
Players will once again work together to complete a series of increasingly difficult objectives inspired by the events of The Return of the King. Every card played matters, every trick counts, and every decision can help (or hinder) The Fellowship’s chances of success.
Prefer to adventure alone? Solo play returns as well, allowing you to tackle Middle-earth’s greatest challenges at your own pace.
And while fans of the previous games will feel right at home, this final chapter introduces new twists and surprises that ensure the journey remains fresh right through to the last hand.

▪️ Wilderness: A Game of Survival (Second Edition) was announced from FryxGames. From the designers of Terraforming Mars, Daniel Fryxelius and Thomas Fryxelius. The first edition Wilderness was their first game back in 2011. From reading about it on the BGG Forums, I see there have been many updates on the original design. Set to be released Q1 of 2027. As early as December for those in Europe. This game plays 1-8 players in about 60-120 minutes.
From the newsletter:

Wilderness can be played as a solo adventure or all the way up to an 8 (!) player race for safety through the hostile jungles, swamps, and deserts! Much is unknown at the start of the game; the randomly selected landscape tiles are face down, the day cards have not yet revealed the coming weather to endure, and surprises from wild animals, sicknesses, and much more are yet to unfold. Your health board will keep track of your special ability as well as your thirst, hunger, and level of exhaustion. At the core, Wilderness is a game about pushing your luck and finding the right balance between managing your health and getting ahead towards that alluring village at the other end of the game board.

▪️ For those in holiday mode looking for a clever gift, you might check out the cool advent calendars like The Walking Dead: The Gift Calendar Game from Mantic Games. There is a new Hellboy one this year for the fans. For 1-4 players and plays in 30 minutes.
From BGG:

Brace yourself for survival in the post-apocalypse this holiday season!
With The Walking Dead: The Gift Calendar Game, each December door unveils a new piece (survivor miniatures, walker miniatures, tokens, dice, and more) until your full survival experience is revealed and the game is ready to play.
In this intense adventure, you must protect your survivors from relentless walker attacks.
Each day, you’ll unlock new components as you prepare to scavenge for supplies and make critical decisions to ensure your group’s survival!
Objective: Players must navigate a Woodbury Training Underground scenario, gathering supplies while fighting off walkers.
Modes: Supports solo play, two-player (survivors vs. walkers), and 3-4 player team survival.

▪️ Québec has a new edition out now from Capstone Games. Originally released in 2011, from designers Pierre Poissant-Marquis & Philippe Beaudoin. This is a very interesting city-building game for 2-5 players and plays in 75 minutes.
From BGG:

By contributing to the numerous buildings, players acquire influence with the authorities of the time: religion, politics, commerce, and culture. Players also help build the famous Citadelle.
During a scoring round at the end of each century, players earn points for the workers they managed to place in the five zones of influence. Québec introduces a unique and addictive majority rule. The player with the majority in a zone cascades half of their workers by moving them to the next zone. Workers moved in this way allow a player to score even more points. If a player still has the majority in the next zone, their workers cascade again – a potentially devastating ripple effect. This mechanism illustrates the interrelationship between the great zones of influence. Players must not only fight to get majorities, but they must also erect the most prestigious buildings.
